Area and channel walk-forward validation

What the results mean

No demonstrated area advantage in this experiment. 1,416 matched forecasts on 127 historical start dates. Pooled Brier score: lognormal 0.1008; area-enhanced 0.1052 (lower is better). Area had a lower score in 4 of 12 line/horizon comparisons; 0 had an improvement interval wholly above zero. Long-horizon evidence is thin: only 9 non-overlapping annual windows per line. Do not use this fixed area rule as a proven trading signal.

Method and limitations

Exploratory historical research—not proof of a trading edge. Automatic channels are refitted on the expanding history ending at each forecast date. No current/full-history channel is projected backward. Both learned models and their scalers use only earlier windows whose outcomes were fully known by that date. The first 60 matured forecast dates train the models; early windows without that history are excluded from ALL matched comparisons. Price targets are fixed at each deadline; a hit is a directional crossing on a later daily adjusted CLOSE, not an intraday touch or a moving-line crossing. The lognormal model estimates continuous-path hits, so its comparison with daily-close hits has a sampling limitation. A 20-session area rectangle is a predeclared research rule, not a backtest of discretionary mouse-drawn boxes or user-selected channel windows. At a fixed window its area is closely related to momentum; it is not independent geometric evidence. The calibrated baseline controls for recalibration alone. Lower Brier score is better; hit rate alone cannot show probability accuracy. Forecasts overlap; non-overlapping results are shown separately. The paired block-bootstrap intervals account approximately for overlapping windows, not all regime dependence, model-selection risk or multiple comparisons. Positive gain means area has lower squared probability error. These dates have been examined in other studies: this is not a fresh untouched holdout. No fees, intraday paths or trading profits are tested. The chart's displayed probability model is not replaced by these exploratory results.

Source: 2010-03-11 through 2026-10-20. 1416 matched forecasts on 127 start dates.
